Performance

Source: vignettes/performance.Rmd
performance.Rmd

This distribution of iCARE has no compiled code. The official version offers a C implementation of its slowest steps (use.c.code = 1, the default); here, the same computations are written as vectorized R, and every workload of the benchmark below runs faster than the official version with its C code.

Benchmark

The script tools/benchmarks/run-benchmarks.R times seven workloads on the example data, with the same inputs in every version:

Workload Description
risk_complete computeAbsoluteRisk(): 10,000 complete covariate profiles, start ages 30-70, intervals of 1-15 years
risk_missing computeAbsoluteRisk(): 2,000 profiles with 15% of covariate values missing
risk_snps computeAbsoluteRisk(): covariates and 72 SNPs with family history, 1,000 profiles with 30% of genotypes missing
split_interval computeAbsoluteRiskSplitInterval(): 2,000 profiles from age 40 to 70, model changing at 50
validation_cohort ModelValidation(): the full cohort (49,767 subjects), risks supplied
validation_ncc ModelValidation(): the nested case-control study (5,240 subjects), risks supplied
validation_internal ModelValidation(): 10,000 cohort subjects, risks computed from the model

The validation workloads use the subjects whose follow-up ends before age 85 (49,767 of the 50,000 cohort members and 5,240 of the 5,285 case-control subjects). The example mortality rates stop at age 85, and the official version gives NA or bin-averaged risks for intervals that end there (see vignette("differences")), so its timings would not be comparable.

Versions compared: this distribution; the official Bioconductor iCARE 1.40.0 with its C code (use.c.code = 1) and without it (use.c.code = 0); and 1.33.1.9002, the patched development version (with its C code). Times are the median elapsed seconds of three runs (one run when the first takes longer than 20 seconds), on an Apple M5 Pro with R 4.6.2 and R’s reference BLAS.

Workload This distribution Official 1.40.0, C code Official 1.40.0, R code 1.33.1.9002, C code Speed-up vs official C
Risks, 10,000 complete profiles 0.17 13.2 51.4 13.8 79.9×
Risks, 2,000 profiles with missing covariates 0.94 2.97 7.63 3.06 3.2×
Risks with 72 SNPs, 1,000 profiles with missing genotypes 7.43 12.2 28.1 11.6 1.6×
Split-interval risks, 2,000 profiles 0.22 0.51 0.48 0.51 2.3×
Validation, full cohort (49,767), risks supplied 0.048 0.96 0.82 1.18 20.0×
Validation, nested case-control (5,240), risks supplied 0.010 0.21 0.21 0.22 20.9×
Validation, 10,000 subjects, risks computed 0.17 0.39 0.38 0.40 2.3×

The largest gains are for complete profiles, whose risks are computed for all profiles and ages at once instead of profile by profile, and for model validation, whose AUC is computed from sorted scores instead of a matrix of all case and non-case pairs. The validation workloads with supplied risks take a few hundredths of a second.

Where the time goes

  • Complete profiles. The cost is one matrix product for the linear predictors and a vectorized pass over the years of age of all intervals; it grows linearly with the number of profiles.
  • Missing risk factors. Profiles are grouped by their pattern of missing risk factors. For each pattern, the reference population is sorted by the linear predictor of the observed risk factors (to form the percentile bins) and each profile’s risk is averaged over its donors. The cost therefore grows with the number of distinct missingness patterns rather than the number of profiles; profiles sharing a pattern cost little more than one.
  • SNPs. With SNPs, the reference population holds n.imp copies of the reference dataset with simulated genotypes (5 × 14,137 rows in the example). Profiles with missing genotypes usually all have different patterns, so each costs one pass over that population: about 7 ms per profile here. Smaller n.imp makes this faster, at the price of more Monte Carlo error in the risks.

For large jobs, pass all profiles to one call: the model (including the calibration of the baseline hazard and the simulated genotypes) is built once per call.

Reproducing the benchmark

From the root of a clone of the repository:

# This distribution, installed into a library of its own
R CMD INSTALL --library=/path/to/lib-dev .
Rscript tools/benchmarks/run-benchmarks.R /path/to/lib-dev refactored

# The official version, installed with
# BiocManager::install("iCARE", lib = "/path/to/lib-official")
Rscript tools/benchmarks/run-benchmarks.R /path/to/lib-official official-c 1
Rscript tools/benchmarks/run-benchmarks.R /path/to/lib-official official-r 0

# A table of all results
Rscript tools/benchmarks/summarize-benchmarks.R

Each version must run in its own R process, because all versions are named iCARE.
